description: The plot illustrates how “Similarity” varies across neural network “Layer” indices for four language-pair conditions shown as separate lines (en&en, en&es, en&el, en&bn). The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0 to 23 with regularly spaced tick labels every 2 layers (0, 2, 4, …, 22). The y-axis is labeled “Similarity,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.00 to 0.45 with tick labels at regular 0.05 intervals. The en&en series is a thick red solid line that starts near 0.07 at layer 0, rises to about 0.26 around layer 6, drops to roughly 0.16 around layer 7–9, stays around ~0.17–0.18 near layers 10–12, declines to about ~0.12 by ~15–16 and ~0.08 by ~19–21, then increases sharply after ~22 to about 0.43 at the final layer. The en&es series is a blue solid line that begins near ~0.06 at layer 0, increases to about ~0.24 around layer 6, falls to ~0.15 around layer 7–9, sits near ~0.17–0.18 around layers 10–12, decreases to roughly ~0.11–0.12 by ~15–16 and ~0.06 by ~20–21, then rises steeply at the end to about ~0.27 at the final layer. The en&el series is a green solid line starting near ~0.05 at layer 0, rising to about ~0.15 around layer 6, dropping to ~0.10 around layer 7–8, increasing gradually to around ~0.14–0.15 near layers 11–12, then declining to about ~0.09 by ~15–16 and ~0.05 by ~19–21, followed by a sharp terminal rise to about ~0.30 at the final layer. The en&bn series is a magenta/pink solid line that starts near ~0.04 at layer 0, climbs to about ~0.14 around layer 6, drops to ~0.10 around layer 7–8, increases to roughly ~0.13–0.14 near layers 11–12, then declines to about ~0.09 by ~15–16 and ~0.05 by ~19–21, before rising sharply at the end to about ~0.29 at the final layer.
